thread.title: Tim Cook Is Hoarding His Apple Stock

author: Ed Lin
title: Tim Cook Is Hoarding His Apple Stock
text:
Illustration: Bloomberg News By Ed Lin July 18, 2018 11:28 a.m. ET Apple shares may not be able to repeat last year’s 48% surge, with shares up only a miserly 14% so far this year, excluding dividend payments. The relative underperformance comes despite raised dividends , record stock buybacks , and the power of Oprah .
Slower Apple (ticker: AAPL) iPhone sales and the company’s status in the ever-hotter U.S.-China trade war has many investors practicing moderation.
Apple executives and directors have been displaying restraint, as well. Company insiders have sold only a quarter of the volume of shares they did by this point last year, 310,370 shares compared with 1.2 million shares in 2017. The dollar value has slowed only to a third, however, to $55.3 million from $165.2 million, due to stock-price appreciation. In all of 2017, Apple insiders sold 1.9 million shares for $271.8 million.
A number of insiders haven’t sold any stock in 2018. Chief Executive Tim Cook by this time last year had sold 138,570 shares for $17 million, and for all of 2017 sold 407,200 shares for $60 million. He hasn’t parted with any of his shares so far this year, however.
Cook has sold shares regularly since 2014 through rule 10b5-1 trading plans, which automatically executes transactions based on price and volume parameters set up by insiders. Planned sales are intended to remove any bias an executive or director would have from knowledge of material nonpublic information. As of Aug. 28, his latest Apple filing , Cook owned 901,500 shares and restricted stock units representing at least 2.94 million shares.
Apple declined to comment on the stock sales.
David Miller , co-founder and chief investment officer of Catalyst Capital Advisors and senior portfolio manager of the Catalyst Insider Buying Fund , suggests Apple insiders are being savvy by refraining from selling now before another stock-repurchase shoe drops. Miller tells Barron’s, “After the tax reform, Apple can bring back a massive amount of overseas profits. They just announced a $100 billion buybac k on May 1 and plan to be cash-neutral—meaning there could be another one again next year.”
Miller adds, “Insiders are aware that [another buyback] should support the stock price. They would be smart to wait and sell once the buybacks are closer to finished.” Miller’s fund doesn’t own Apple shares, but the Catalyst Buyback Strategy Fund does.
Eddy Cue , senior vice president of internet software and services, hasn’t sold any Apple stock so far in 2018. Cue, who oversees the iTunes Store, Apple Music, and Apple Pay , by this time last year sold 45,000 shares for $6.9 million. For all of last year, he told a total of $18.1 million in stock, 110,360 shares. The sales were made through a trust that Cue controls. As of April 3 , Cue owned 65,370 shares through the trust and held restricted stock units representing at least 113,170 shares.
Former Vice President Al Gore hasn’t sold any Apple shares in 2018, after selling 285,437 shares for $38.4 million in February 2017. Although he joined Apple’s board as a director in 2003 , Gore hasn’t sold stock before those transactions—or since. As of Feb. 8 , Gore owned 44,175 Apple shares.
Apple director Andrea Jung , president and CEO of microfinance firm Grameen America and former CEO of Avon Products (AVP), sold 100,000 shares for $12.8 million in February 2017 but has sold none so far this year. She joined Apple’s board in 2008. As of Feb. 5 , Jung owned 21,000 Apple shares.
Craig Federighi , Apple’s senior vice president of software engineering, sold 198,290 shares for $29.4 million in 2017, with 135,130 shares sold, for $19.5 million, by this point last year. The head of the development of iOS and MacOS hasn’t sold any stock in 2018, however. As of April 3 , Federighi owned 460,370 shares and restricted stock units representing at least 113,170 shares.
Angela Ahrendts , senior vice president of retail, has sold 44,800 shares for $8 million year to date, compared with 100,380 shares sold, for $15 million, by this time last year and a total of 163,765 shares sold, for $24.8 million, in 2017. Ahrendts, whose sales were planned transactions, oversees Apple’s physical stores, its online store, and its contact centers. As of June 18 , Ahrendts owned 66,350 shares.
Johny Srouji , senior vice president of hardware technologies, has sold 15,000 Apple shares for $2.8 million year to date, compared with 49,460 shares for $7 million in the year-ago period. Srouji sold a total of 76,500 shares for $11.5 million in all of 2017. As of May 25 , he owned 73,300 shares directly and another 2,000 shares indirectly through his children and a trust.
In addition to holding off for a higher stock price, there could be another reason for the diminished insider selling. It’s possible that the price of Apple shares haven’t risen high enough to meet the preset selling prices in trading plans. Whatever the reasons, some insiders are at or above the same level of sales they were in the year-ago period, including a few who use trading plans.
Luca Maestri , Apple’s chief financial officer , has maintained the dollar value of his stock transactions, selling 43,900 shares for $7.7 million so far in 2018, compared with 53,280 shares sold for $7.6 million a year ago, all of which were sold by early June 2017. Maestri’s sales were planned transactions. As of June 4 , he owned 63,375 shares.
Dan Riccio , senior vice president of hardware engineering, has sold 50,400 shares for $8.9 million so far this year, compared with 58,740 shares sold for $8.5 million in the year-ago period and a total of 105,660 shares sold for $16.2 million in 2017. Riccio, who leads the Mac, iPhone, iPad, and iPod engineering teams , made his sales through planned transactions. As of May 21 , he owned 34,740 shares.
Chairman Arthur D. Levinson has sold 35,000 Apple shares for $6.5 million year to date, compared with 37,600 shares sold for $5.7 million in the year-ago period and a total of 72,600 shares sold for $11.2 million in 2017. Levinson is the former chairman and CEO of Genentech . As of May 11 , he owned 1.1 million Apple shares directly, another 14,000 through a spouse, and restricted stock units representing at least 35,000 shares.
A trust controlled by Philip W. Schiller , senior vice president of worldwide marketing, has sold 69,500 Apple shares for $11.6 million so far in 2018, compared with 47,800 shares sold for $6.9 million in the year-ago period and a total of 104,600 shares sold for $15.6 million in 2017. Schiller’s sales were planned transactions. As of April 5 , he owned 49,575 shares through a trust.
Apple’s Chief Operating Officer Jeff Williams , who oversees development of the Apple Watch , has begun shares after hoarding them last year. Williams has sold 46,960 shares for $8.9 million so far this year; he last sold stock in 2016, a total of 338,700 shares that year for $36.6 million, and had been selling on a regular basis from 2011 to that year. His sales were planned transactions. As of July 11 , he owned 123,740 shares.
Chris Kondo , Apple’s principal accounting officer, has sold 4,870 shares for $910,130 so far this year, compared with 2,650 shares sold for $339,200 in the year-ago period and a total of 8,860 shares sold for $1.3 million in 2017. As of May 18 , Kondo owned 8,430 shares.
Bruce Sewell , who retired as Apple’s general counsel at the end of last year, sold 174,125 shares for $24.7 million in 2017. As he is no longer a company officer, he is no longer obligated to disclose sales of Apple stock. As of Oct. 3 , Sewell owned 172,265 shares, but he could sell them all without further public notice.
Editor’s Note: This article has been updated to reflect that the company has declined to comment.
